Upstream lands weekly (standing rule 5) — also implement the per-workstream 'check upstream activity first' step. First cold runner build compiles LLVM (hours); disk cache makes later builds incremental. LANDED at UA-1 (fork/upstream/plan.md rev 3; decision-log entry 'Upstream advance 2026-10: cut 631f8fb -> c1e83b0b7 (2026-10-06)'): the staging flow as it now runs under R28 -- a plan with two adversarial reviews and a focused re-review, a staging branch cut from trunk (claude/carbon-fork-0-1-upstream-advance), one merge commit carrying every textual and semantic resolution by conflict class (A keep both, B re-express the fork mechanism inside upstream's structure, C adopt upstream's and keep the fork's goldens and programs as pins), a separately revertible class-C deletion commit, a mechanical reflow commit under R31's heading/list-count detectors, hosted fills to a fixpoint with a retriage commit per `Problems that require manual fixes` list, one fix commit per defect naming its root cause, the pre-merge scoreboard against trunk's floor, a true merge of trunk back into the staging branch before discharge, gate + conformance of record, and a discharge commit (decision-log entry with the divergence-risk register review, ORCHESTRATION, ledger). Measured: 183 commits, 105 conflicts (31 sources/docs + 74 goldens), five hosted fill passes (two crashed and were root-caused, three pushed 225/22/12 goldens), four fix/triage rounds, pre-merge 126/0/23 over 149 (run 37399118672) = trunk's pre-SL-2 floor exactly. The recurring weekly check (standing rule 5) is the Routine 'Weekly upstream-merge check (carbon fork)', which measures from `git merge-base` and needed no edit (D-UA-13). Item stays open only for the per-workstream 'check upstream activity first' step, which the plans already perform by hand (plan section 0 audits); close at UA-2 if no automation is wanted.

Mechanism (plan §2.4 as pre-declared, digest item 4; narrowed post-review B-1, 2026-08-18): the call-argument path — `InventPrimitiveClangArg` calling `TryMapFunctionType` directly, and ONLY that path; `TryMapType`/`MapToCppType` return null for function types so export-direction consumers (exported return types, exported globals) keep the pre-F8d 'failed to map' diagnosis instead of pairing a function value's empty runtime representation with an 8-byte function pointer — maps a concrete non-generic non-member function's `SemIR::FunctionType` to a pointer to its exported declaration's C++ type (`GetOrExportFunctionDeclToCpp`, check/cpp/export.cpp, reusing the reverse-interop `Carbon::F` export the F8a bridge programs already exercise); the invented Clang argument is an AST-embedded `DeclRefExpr` + `CK_FunctionToPointerDecay` (the constant.cpp constexpr shape), so Sema deduces e.g. `std::thread`'s ctor template on `void(*)()`; the resolved signature records the embedded declaration (`ClangDeclSignature::constant_function_args`, part of the canonical signature key so different functions passed to one callee import separately), no Carbon parameter is formed for it, the runtime argument is dropped at the call (check/cpp/call.cpp), and the C++ thunk embeds the reference in its body instead of taking a parameter, with the constant's mangled name appended to the thunk symbol to keep same-signature thunks distinct (check/cpp/thunk.cpp). Upstreamable. items.notes: DISCHARGED (fork/overload/plan.md OV-3, 2026-10-05; branch claude/carbon-fork-0-1-ov3, cut from trunk ae157438d with OV-2 and UN-2 merged; commits 13aa792bc the generate_ast.cpp export arm + goldens + conformance + ledger, 4033adc75 docs, 3a7bc00d3 implementation-review fixes; hosted fills 88b863220 and 37346182494 (refill after the review fixes), 37353176048 on the trunk merge (SL-1 in; one id line in the AST dump moved, which exposed an unnormalized Clang id at end of line — fixed in the file_test autoupdater) and 37355767908 (converged)): C++ name lookup of a Carbon `overload fn` set (`MapInstIdToClangDeclOrType`, `OverloadSetValue` arm) exports every member in declaration order through the unchanged per-function path (`GetOrExportFunctionToCpp` → `ExportFunctionToCpp`, keyed on each member's `first_decl_id()`) and hands Clang the list of non-null results as one overload set (`SetExternalVisibleDeclsForName` already took a list), so C++ callers resolve under C++ rules while Carbon callers resolve by declaration-order first-match — the documented divergence of F-009, conformance-tested in both directions (§5.C: the agreeing `Describe` set, `i32`/`bool`, EXPECT 1 2 2 1; the diverging `Pick` set, `i64` first, `i32` second: Carbon 1 by widening, C++ 2 by exact match). Members in class scope export as C++ member-function overloads of the exported class (`method_set`, `ref self` members lvalue-ref-qualified); a member whose signature has no C++ mapping is dropped after the existing per-function semantics TODO — an error, so the unit is rejected until the member maps; the mappable members are still delivered to Clang, so the TODO is the only diagnostic and no `no member named` cascade follows (sub-fork F-009i, `fail_todo_partial_export`); an empty list is the single-function nullptr outcome. Zero new diagnostics. Deviations from the plan, recorded: (1) R-10's falsifier FIRED — the per-member Carbon thunk (`F__carbon_thunk`, a generated function that is NOT a set member, so D-OV-5's `:overload<N>` marker never reached it) mangled identically for every member, and lowering's `GetOrCreateFunction` would have reused the first member's thunk for the second (lower/file_context.cpp `getFunction(mangled_name)` early return); the D-OV-9 fallback applies: ONE additive hunk in export.cpp `BuildCarbonToCarbonThunk` propagates the member's `overload_index` onto the generated thunk `Function` right after `MakeGeneratedFunctionDecl` (the set-relative index, declaration order, stable across files; `overload_set_id` stays unset, so the mangler's set-agreement CHECK does not apply), so the mangler keys the thunk as it keys the member and a member's thunk symbol is `_CF__carbon_thunk:overload<N>.Main` — `:` is unspellable in a Carbon identifier, so no user function can collide with it — and its C++ declaration's asm label names it (the first cut, 13aa792bc, suffixed the thunk NAME with `__overload<N>`, which a user `fn F__carbon_thunk__overload1` could collide with; replaced by the review's root fix in 3a7bc00d3 — decision-log D-OV-17); plan §0.2 item 7's "touches NONE of W-007's three files" is therefore false by one hunk, after UN-2 merged as D-OV-9 requires. (2) The omitted-member TODO is `failed to map C++ type to Carbon` (export.cpp `BuildCppToCarbonThunkFunctionType`, the thunk-signature path that runs first), not §4.C's predicted `failed to map Carbon type to C++`; the pin uses a tuple-typed parameter `(i32, i32)` rather than the plan's `choice`, because a choice is a `ClassType` that `TryMapClassType` exports as a C++ class (type_mapping.cpp, the `ExportClassToCpp` fallthrough) and so is not unmappable. (3) §4.C's `partial_export` subfile is `fail_todo_partial_export`: its omitted member emits the semantics TODO, and file_test requires the `fail_` prefix on an erroring subfile (so §4.C's "`fail_todo_...`: none" is off by this one). (4) §4.C's "`imports` block showing both exported thunks" is not what a `--dump-sem-ir-ranges=only` check golden shows — the exported thunks are generated functions outside the dumped ranges — so the check golden pins the Carbon side's selections and the diagnostics, and the lower twin pins the C++ side's callee symbols (the two different `_CPick:overload<N>.Main` callees in one golden). Plan §0.2 item 3 applies (design README:3878-3881, not :3822) and item 7 is amended as in (1). The bidirectional-assertion rule is fork/rulebook.md R30 (allocated at this discharge, the next free number after R29), citing cpp_export_overload_set_divergence.carbon as its precedent. Prior hand-offs: OV-2 hand-off (2026-10-05): W-025 landed and §1.B.5's generic-scope lifting HELD (no residue), so OV-3's target for the gap row is DONE, not the PARTIAL fallback. OV-1 hand-off (2026-09-28): W-024 landed; the W-007 edge stayed until OV-3 per D-OV-9 and is cleared here (the additive-hunk record goes in W-007's notes at discharge). Original filing: Loop the set through ExportFunctionToCpp; C++ callers resolve with C++ rules — Carbon-first-match vs C++-best-match divergence is accepted and conformance-tested in both directions (rulebook rule proposed in paper). Docs stage also fills interoperability/README.md:210 empty TODO and retires the design README:3822 placeholder. Review record: one implementation review (R29(c)) APPROVE-WITH-FIXES — MAJOR 1 the "exportable subset stays callable" overclaim at three sites (reworded; decision-log D-OV-18: the unit is rejected), MINOR 2 the identifier-spellable thunk-name suffix (replaced by the `overload_index` propagation, D-OV-17), MINOR 3 `method_set` pinned only by "it compiled" (overload_set_ast.carbon and a lower `method_set` subfile added), MINOR 4 the gap row and header flipped ahead of the of-record run (stamped from the run at this discharge), MINOR 5 one TODO per member for generic-class sets (pinned by `fail_todo_generic_class_set`; filed W-117, D-OV-20), MINOR 6 two members with one C++ signature (filed W-118; no belt added). The divergence is documented, not bridged (D-OV-19): no export-side coherence check, no `.diff.cpp` sibling for either §5.C program. items.notes: The one genuinely new subsystem: diagnostic capture around deferred-action replay, generalizing the existing impl_lookup diagnose=false idiom — the irreducible cost of any predicate-supporting option. Absorbs Option C's `where <bool-expr>` binding form. Spec the probe subsystem ONCE and have overloading's candidate loop (W-025) consume it too (coherence risk 4). B2 and W7's deferred-action completion should be one engineering track (structural-conformance.md:527-532). Probe-observability rule is user open question 4. OV-1 (2026-09-28, fork/overload/plan.md §8.5): the overload candidate probe (toolchain/check/call.cpp `PerformCallToOverloadSet`, :475) uses the `DeduceImplArguments` discard idiom (deduce.cpp) extended with a cleanup-depth snapshot and `DiscardCleanupsSince` (:464) plus `TryConvertToValueOfType`; a shared probe subsystem would replace both call sites. Probes are not diagnostic-free (W-104). SC-1 (2026-10-12): W-027 landed on branch (fill pending), blocked_by edge cleared. SC-1 fill round 7 (2026-10-14): a template constraint's `Self` is a checked-phase binding again (fork/structural/plan.md D-SC-10, its break condition taken; toolchain/check/handle_named_constraint.cpp:128-135), so the template phase that definition-time checking needs to defer the checks that involve `Self` (docs/design/generics/template_constraints.md, Definition-time checking) is a prerequisite of this item: flip it with the probe subsystem, re-running round 6's review-1 BLOCKER-1 probes (an alias of `Self` and declarations nested in a template constraint, named with no self type from non-template code). SC-1 fill round 8 (2026-10-14): the checked-phase `Self` is kept as a trade (fork/decision-log.md ROUND 8's DECISION). The template phase is what restores the requirement signatures W-169 files (`typeof(Self.N)*`, `Self.A` naming the satisfying type's own `A`, `Box(Self)` for `class Box(T: J)`, `Self.(J.Elem)`, `Core.Slice(Self)`, `Core.Optional(Self)`; since fill round 9 the `fail_todo_` splits of check/testdata/named_constraint/template_constraint.carbon hold each with the class that satisfied it through fill round 6 and its use, to become positive), and its flip must keep a `require` whose facet type takes `Self` as an argument accepted (template_constraint_require.carbon `require_self_argument` and `fail_require_self_argument_unsatisfied`, lower/testdata/template/template_constraint.carbon `require_self_argument`), which the template-phase `Self` of rounds 1 to 6 rejected as a splice; if it cannot, the phase is scoped to the validity blocks' own checks rather than to the constraint's `Self`. It must also keep an overload probe silent for a type that does not satisfy a `Self`-dependent requirement signature: through fill round 6 the template-phase `Self` made that a hard "unable to monomorphize" error even in a probe and with `require impls J` (round 8's review 1 probes b01 to b04 on fb12f63cb), against SC-1's D-SC-12; pinned by `self_facet_in_signature_required`'s overload set `P` and lower/testdata/template/template_constraint.carbon `overload_probe_require` (SC-1 fill round 9), which this item's probe subsystem must keep passing. items.notes: Merges three scanner reports. call.cpp:127 'unsupported type used as template argument' WAS the blocker the gap-analysis cited at filing (MapToCppType had no mapping for a symbolic Carbon type); upstream PR 7673 lifted it (the instantiation is a deferred `CallCppTemplateAction`, instantiated per specific since PR 7700) and the TODO, now call.cpp:133, is reached only for a CONCRETE type `MapToCppType` cannot map (corrected at UA-2 round 3, 2026-10-12); :252 restricts non-type template parameter arguments; type_mapping.cpp:560 TODOs form-dependent (template-dependent) args to C++ functions. Fix direction per both conformance SKIPs: defer C++ template instantiation to monomorphization (hence the W-014 dependency and W8 grouping). One blocker, two scoreboard entries under two bullets: cpp_template_symbolic_arg.carbon (owning bullet) and cpp_template_on_carbon_generic.carbon (bullet: Type system: C++ interop — importing C++ types / exporting Carbon types). Concrete Carbon class types as template args already work per the PASSing cpp_template_carbon_class.carbon... (verify: gap-analysis says Carbon class types error; conformance shows concrete-class PASS on the 2026.07.19 toolchain — re-check which sub-case is live before claiming). UA-2 (2026-10-06): the round-1 probes COMPILE-FAILED on hosted conformance 37407530104 with (1) `ConversionFailureTypeToFacet` "cannot convert type `<splice of <cannot stringify inst...: {kind: ConvertToValueAction, ...}>>` into type implementing `Core.DefaultOrUnformed`" at the uninitialized `var b: Cpp.Box(T);` and (2) "unable to monomorphize specific" / "cannot copy value of type `Point`" at `b.value = v;`. Root cause by evidence, not a fork regression: both reproduce on upstream nightly 2026.09.28+1579d4e, and (1) reproduces there on upstream's EXACT pin shape (`fn F[T: type](unused x: T) { var unused v: Cpp.S(T); }`) under the real prelude -- the pin passes in file_test only because min_prelude/parts/default.carbon:19 declares an unconstrained blanket `DefaultOrUnformed` impl where the real prelude's (core/prelude/default.carbon:52) requires `T: UnformedInit`, undecidable for a template-dependent self; the fork's deltas in convert.cpp (union/choice/overload-set conversions) and impl_lookup.cpp (a comment) do not touch the facet-conversion path, and the fork's refill of generic_call.carbon is byte-identical to upstream's. (2) is a program bug: a Carbon class is not implicitly `Core.Copy`. Programs edited (headers record it): the box is initialized through its C++ default constructor (`Cpp.Box(T).Box()`, upstream's class/import/template.carbon:149 shape) and the Carbon class declares `impl as Core.Copy`; verified end to end on the 2026.09.28 nightly (compile, link, run `7`). The claim is unchanged (`Cpp.Box(T)` with symbolic `T` in the body and the return type), so the item's remaining scope is the uninitialized-dependent-`var` limit (an upstream limitation, pinned) and the W-014 pattern-splice/cross-file residue; blocked_by W-014 kept. UA-2 round 3 (2026-10-12; implementation review MAJOR-1, MAJOR-4 and MINOR-6 folded): MEASURED -- both programs PASS, `7` each, on hosted conformance 37413300832 (of record, scoreboard 131 PASS / 0 FAIL / 19 SKIP over 150, 48/56 bullets; run 37411196881 measured the same numbers and lost its scoreboard push to the fill's push). The real-prelude uninitialized-dependent-`var` limit is now its own item, W-127: its removal condition (impl lookup deferring a template-dependent self under a constrained blanket impl) is unrelated to W-014's template lowering, so W-014 was never the right gate for it. This item keeps only the W-014 residue behind the two programs' claim (pattern splices, cross-file template lowering); blocked_by W-014 unchanged. The nightly-2026.09.28 reproduction above ran in a container that has since been recreated; its command and output were not written down and are not reproducible from this tree -- the structural proof (default.carbon:52 against parts/default.carbon:19) is the evidence of record, carried by W-127. DD-1 (2026-10-13) answers the verify note: a concrete Carbon class as a C++ template argument compiles and runs (P17, `Cpp.Box(Point)`); the symbolic case fails without an initializer (probe PR-T); gap row 56's sentence on class types is stale (plan §0.4 item 8). DD-1's second document-review fold (2026-10-14, R2-2) corrects the symbolic half: with an initializer, as in `let b: Cpp.Box(T) = Cpp.Box(T).Make(x);` in a function with a checked parameter `[T: Core.Copy]`, a checked generic's type parameter is a C++ template argument and the template is instantiated for each specific, on the fork toolchain and the nightly 2026.10.12 (fork/designdocs/samples/X09_cpp_template_symbolic_arg.carbon prints `7 8 4`); PR-T fails only because its `var unused b: Cpp.Box(T);` has no initializer (``cannot convert type `<splice of ...>` into type implementing `Core.DefaultOrUnformed` ``), the limit docs/design/interoperability/README.md:664-667 now states. For this item's owner: the SKIP reason of fork/conformance/programs/interop/cpp_template_symbolic_arg.carbon ("unsupported type used as template argument" at `var b: Cpp.Box(T);`, measured on the nightly 2026.07.19) is stale; on the fork toolchain and the nightly 2026.10.12 its first error is that missing initializer, and `b.value = v;` then fails because `Point` is not `Core.Copy` (``cannot copy value of type `Point` ``) LAND-1 (2026-11-02): the SKIP of fork/conformance/programs/interop/cpp_template_symbolic_arg.carbon that DD-1's sentence above calls stale was removed by PR 51 (UA-2 round 1), which landed before PR 58. DISCHARGED at CT-1 (2026-11-02, fork/cpp-templates/plan.md): the blocker the item names, a symbolic Carbon type as a C++ template argument, had been lifted upstream (PRs 7673, 7689 and 7700: a deferred `CallAction` over `TemplateInst`-wrapped arguments); fifteen defects in and around that path kept it from working (impl lookup on the specialization resolved where the generic is defined, so an uninitialized `var` of it was rejected; C++ actions performed for a symbolic specific; action operands not substituted; a narrow scalar `return` given a return slot; variable template specializations never instantiated; an exported Carbon class queried before it was complete; an alias's value detached from its enclosing generic; an enclosing generic's operand kept in a member's action; an alias's name reference not followed to its value; an alias's template-dependent value converted and checked where it is written, not in each specific; a use of such an alias through a concrete specific given the generic's category, not the specific's, a nested alias's use included; a deferred store's temporary typed in the generic, not the specific; a deferred C++ call's `ref` argument not unwrapped in the specific; a class template's specialization formed for a checked generic's argument not deferring its impl lookup), each fixed at its root, and a C++ call with a checked generic's symbolic argument is deferred to each specific, a fork rule (F-021). The two SKIP programs run without their SKIP lines and with the `Core.Copy` impl each needs, keeping the uninitialized `var b: Cpp.Box(T);`. Measured in the container (EXPECTED, not of record, R9): 1978 of 1978, conformance 189 / 0 / 15 over 204. The evidence's type_mapping.cpp TODO (:560 when filed, :733-736 at CT-1) is live and filed as W-307, and call.cpp:252's non-type restriction (:252 when filed, the TODO at :246 and :256-259 at CT-1's head) as W-302. Residues: W-300 (struct, tuple and unexportable class types), W-301 (Carbon generics as template template arguments), W-302 (non-type argument kinds), W-303 (deduction through a C++ specialization, in a parameter's type or an impl's self), W-304 (a concrete C++ class `var` in a template's body stops lowering), W-305 (interface member access through a constraint on a specialization's member), W-306 (instantiation notes without a line, repeated E-MONO), W-307 (form-dependent arguments to C++ functions), W-308 (C++ classes as choice payloads), W-309 (a deferred call's C++ temporary not destroyed), W-310 (a `returned var` of a specialization), W-311 (a `returned var` of a symbolic type stops lowering, upstream's); CT-1's forms work within one library, and a use from another library stays W-250's. Focused re-review, round 1 (2026-10-22): two reviews of the fold and these records at 118fc1bc8 both returned APPROVE-WITH-FIXES with no BLOCKER or MAJOR and twelve MINOR records findings, all folded and none rejected, with no fix commit and no residue filed, so the round is dry and the loop ends (fork/cpp-templates/plan.md, 'Focused re-review of the fold, round 1 (2026-10-22)'). (LAND-1, 2026-11-02: the "not of record" label above is superseded by PR 64's landing's container-measured scoreboard, R33 (b), 189/0/15 over 204 with 49/56 bullets.)

What landed: IMPORT — `CustomCppTypeMapping` is a struct with an element-type payload; the `StdSpan` matcher accepts `span` in `std` with a type argument and an all-ones integral extent (`std::dynamic_extent`), so `std::span<T, 3>` fails it and imports as an ordinary class; `LookupCustomRecordType` maps the match to `Core.Slice(T')` through `MakeSliceType` over `ImportCppType(T)`, so `std::span<const int>` is `Core.Slice(const i32)` (D-SL-8). EXPORT — `RecognizedTypeInfo::Slice` (a Core-root class named `Slice` with one argument) and the `Slice` arm of type_mapping.cpp's exhaustive switch: a `WrappedType` instantiating `std::span` found by name on the recursively mapped element type; a TU without `<span>` maps to the null type and the existing `SemanticsTodo` `failed to map Carbon type to C++` reports it — no new diagnostic kind (D-SL-8). OWNING -> VIEW — `CoreInterface::CppContiguousRange` synthesized from member `data()` + `size()` (const overload preferred, no ADL), the public prelude helpers (`CppContiguousRange`, `CppDataPointer`, `CppSizeToI64`, the constraint `CppContiguous`; `private` in the plan sketch, public since round 1 because slice.carbon's impl names them) and the blanket `ImplicitAs(Slice(C.Element))` impl with the two-step `ImplicitAs(u64)` then `As(i64)` size conversion (D-SL-9, rev A A2), so `let view: Core.Slice(const i32) = v;` and `Cpp.SumSpan(v)` work for a `Cpp.std.vector(i32)`. Goldens mock `std::span` (D-SL-14); conformance uses the real `<span>` with `COMPILE-ARGS: --clang-arg=-std=c++20` and pins the 16-byte layout premise (R-6) with a `static_assert` in both programs. The first hosted fill (run 37356848697, 0790c7428) refuted it: the blanket impl is an orphan there (impl_validation.cpp `DiagnoseOrphanImpl` walks the self type and the interface specific for a class of the same library -- `Slice` is slice.carbon's; the facet-type bound on the self binding does not count) and, independently, impl lookup imports candidates only from the IRs owning the query's self/interface/arguments (impl_lookup.cpp `FindAssociatedImportIRs`), so the impl would never have been a candidate; two more errors followed (`Destroy` for the `Data()`/`Size()` temporaries, which a synthesized witness's bare-`type` associated constants cannot carry). Landed layout: the helpers stay in cpp/slice.carbon as PUBLIC Core names (`CppUnsafeDeref` precedent) plus `CppSizeToI64`; slice.carbon's reserved `optional` import line imports cpp/slice at the same line count; the impl is appended beside `Slice` with `require ... & Destroy` on the constraint. Zero DI churn; the impls still use only the public `Slice` API (`UnsafeMake`). (2) The static-extent golden names `std::span<int, 3>` through a header alias `IntSpan3` (the class/import/template.carbon `using Ai32 = A<int>` spelling) rather than the plan's `Cpp.std.span(i32, 3)`: no golden instantiates a C++ class template with a non-type argument from Carbon, so the alias is the R3 spelling. Residue filed: W-119 static-extent `std::span` mapping (D-SL-8), W-120 ADL `data`/`size` sources for `CppContiguousRange` (§1.B.3); 'owning C++ container to Core.Slice view' is NOT filed (the D-SL-9 chain resolved at the second fill, 18e2165c1 -- vector_view.carbon's `view` split shows the synthesized witness and the blanket impl selected -- and the conformance run of record 37390640614 (on affa54e8a, which the final head differs from only by the scoreboard commit 2a17f0239 and the CHECK-only convergence commit) arbitrates it at runtime; R-9's contingency — the deducible-parameter spelling `impl forall [E: Copy & Destroy, C: CppContiguous where .Element = E] C as ImplicitAs(Slice(E))` — is recorded in vector_view.carbon's comment). Risks for the fill, in order: R-9 (the projection `C.Element` in the interface argument list; its in-tree precedent is impl/lookup/access.carbon:26 `T as X(T.Z1.(Y.Y1))`, recorded at the round-1 fix -- the primary spelling is kept, fold B9 not applied), R-10 (`Cpp.std.vector(i32)` importing from the real libc++), R-7 (`std::span` lookup through the inline namespace), and the SL-1 lesson that a new prelude impl of `ImplicitAs` may leave import traces in goldens that perform `ImplicitAs` lookups over the full prelude. ROUND-1 FIX (2026-10-05, after run 37356848697 moved 306 files and the implementation review's REJECT -- 1 BLOCKER, 3 MAJOR, 5 MINOR): BLOCKER = deviation (1) above, fixed by the zero-churn relocation; MAJOR 2 = `LookupCppMemberWithResultType`'s `CARBON_CHECK` on the result type was an ICE for `void data(); void size();` and for an unmappable result -- fixed to decline/propagate, and fail_vector_view.carbon gains `fail_void_members`. What landed, by D-OP number: D-OP-1 equality (two empty values are equal, an empty and a non-empty value are not, two non-empty values compare as `T`'s `==`, and `!=` is `T`'s `!=`); D-OP-2 ordering with only `Ordered` required (an empty value orders before every non-empty one); D-OP-3 the spelling `final impl forall [T: Destroy & OptionalStorage & Eq] Optional(T) as EqWith(Optional(T))` and its `Ordered` twin, `final`; D-OP-4 bodies over `HasValue()` and `Get()`, no builtin and no storage-interface change, running `T.Copy` and `T.Destroy` once per value when both operands hold one (a divergence from comparison_operators.md:316 and :434 that F-015 discloses); D-OP-5 same-type comparisons only; D-OP-6 F-015, docs/design/optional.md, with the placeholder TODO kept under a dated amendment line (:27); D-OP-7 SF-9's KEEP stands and `Optional` stays a class; D-OP-8 no existing line of optional.carbon moves (0 of 1942 goldens changed); D-OP-9 min_prelude unchanged; D-OP-10 three new goldens; D-OP-11 optional_missing_ops SKIP -> PASS, three new PASS programs, four write-tests-first SKIPs; D-OP-12 payload destruction is not OP-1's (W-170); D-OP-13 the row stays PARTIAL; D-OP-14 the page and three dated amendments; D-OP-15 the merge position (last, after PR 55). The `Try` impl :56-78 unchanged (SF-9 KEEP): its signature `final impl forall [T: Destroy & OptionalStorage] Optional(T) as Try where .ContinueType = T and .BreakType = ()` and its body are exactly EH-A's. Residues, filed at this discharge: W-170 a `Core.Optional` never destroys the value it holds (row-bounding); W-171 the default storage mis-lowers `MaybeUnformed(T) unsafe as T` when `T`'s value representation differs (`Core.Optional(bool)`'s `Get()` and copy crash the compiler, `Core.Optional(Core.Optional(U*))`'s return wrong values; row-bounding); W-172 a float or character literal argument for a `T: Core.Copy & Core.Destroy` parameter aborts check in `CanDestroyType`; W-173 `Core.Optional(T).Get()` on an empty value is unchecked; W-174 the prelude gives built-in pointer types no `==`; W-175 no explicit `as` between Optionals; W-176 `Core.Optional(T)` requires `T: Copy & Destroy` (or a pointer) through the private `OptionalStorage`; W-177 `Core.Optional` is not matchable; W-178 the `like` operator is not parsed; W-179 a non-final impl that a `final` impl completely subsumes is diagnosed only where it is used; W-195 a checked generic body that applies a compile-time-only operation to a symbolic `T` aborts lowering (the plan's W-190, re-allocated at the discharge re-scan because DD-1's plan reserves W-180..W-194). Coherence risk 9 of W-006 is resolved the other way (D-OP-7): Optional's design landed outside W5 with the class kept; W-006, W-010, W-011 and W-049 carry OP-1 notes. items.notes: Merges the clang_runtimes diagnostic item: CARBON_FATAL('Target architecture is not supported') for any non-x86/ARM triple (with an adjacent CHECK rejecting 16-bit x86) should become a user-facing diagnostic — a small fix inside this workstream. clang_runtimes.cpp hard-errors on Windows, LLD is wired for ELF/MachO only, no Windows CI, releases Linux-x86-64-only. Arbiter: Windows CI runner installing the toolchain, building runtimes, compiling/linking/executing a Carbon+C++-interop program, plus released artifacts for Windows/macOS/Linux incl. arm64. Independent of language features. Must budget the MSVC-funclet EH variant of the W-016/W-019 thunk fencing (error-handling.md:540-542). EH-A (2026-09-27): the `Result`-returning entry point's `.Err` epilogue calls POSIX `write(2)` directly (toolchain/lower/handle.cpp:344-356, declared through getOrInsertFunction like the `printf` precedent) — the Windows port needs an equivalent (fork/eh/plan.md R-5). EH-B (2026-09-27): the fence diagnostic's `__carbon_boundary_write` is a second POSIX `write(2)` dependency (toolchain/check/cpp/thunk.cpp:121-154), and the MSVC-funclet variant of the fence must also carry the catching thunk (`BuildCppCatchingThunk`, thunk.cpp:1135) and the `__cxa_current_primary_exception` capture, which is Itanium-only. macOS (V-1, not exercised by the Linux hosted gate): synthesized asm labels are emitted literally, so the thunk decls take `getUserLabelPrefix()` (`write`) or `extern "C"` linkage (`__cxa_current_primary_exception`); libc++ on Apple does not re-export `__cxa_rethrow_primary_exception` (libcxxabi/lib/symbols-not-reexported.exp), so C++ consumers of `<carbon/expected.h>` calling `Exception::ptr()`/`rethrow()` link `-lc++abi` there (header comment; a Darwin link of cpp_exception_rethrow_export failing on an undefined `___cxa_*` symbol is the falsifier). EV-1 (2026-10-13, fork/evaluator/plan.md section 0.1 row 15): cross-targeting Windows from Linux, measured on 0.0.0-0.dev+0bdce60a5 and on nightly 0.0.0-0.nightly.2026.10.12: `carbon compile --target=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` fails with `error: unsupported option '-fPIE' for target 'x86_64-pc-windows-msvc'` (exit 1); `carbon link` with that target prints the same error and then a crash stack dump (exit 134 on the fork toolchain), on both toolchains alike — upstream behavior. docs/guides/getting_started.md labels Windows unsupported (clang_runtimes.cpp:240-242) and names WSL 2 as the route docs/project/contribution_tools.md:169-176 documents, not measured.

items.notes: Scope cut recorded from the W4 slice-1 adversarial review (finding F3): `match (n) { case 5 => {A} case 5 => {B} default => {} }` compiles cleanly with a dead second arm. Runtime SemIR is still design-correct (top-down first-match-wins, pattern_matching.md:694-695,745-747), so this is a missing diagnostic, not a mischeck; the design requires 'We will diagnose... A pattern is not useful in the context of prior patterns.' RF-4's constant-expression admission creates invisible overlaps (for example `case 5` vs `case 2 + 3` on the same scrutinee), so duplicate/overlap detection must compare evaluated constant values, not source forms. BLOCKER DISCHARGED at W8a (fork/w008/plan.md §3.4; W8a verified 2026-09-25): W8a fixed the value domain usefulness comparisons need — tuple constant vectors and alternative index + payload constants. W-066 is startable; W8b/W8c gate nothing here. Mechanism: BuildMatchCaseUsefulnessKey (pattern_match.cpp) keys arms as Wildcard/IntConst(IntId)/Alternative(index,payloads)/Tuple preorder vectors; IntId equality is exact value comparison (int.h mathematical-value canonicalization) so `case 5` == `case 2 + 3`; first-covering-prior slot-wise subsumption plus the step-3b choice-root union-coverage check (rides covered_alternatives' irrefutable-payload semantics) in EmitCaseArmTestAndBind before the coverage block; diagnostics MatchCaseNeverMatches + MatchCaseNeverMatchesPriorArm/-FullCoverage. items.notes: Scope trade recorded at fork/match-replatform/plan.md §3.4 and re-recorded at the S2d landing: design authority allows `default if (E) => ...` (so `default` stays equivalent to `case _: auto`), but the fork's parser attaches guard nodes only to `case` — `HandleMatchDefaultIntroducer` goes straight to the handler block with no guard production. The check side is small once parse carries the nodes: a guarded `default` arm reuses the S2d capture-splice-branch shape with no pattern test and no bindings, and its else edge needs a following arm or another `default` to fall through to, so the exhaustiveness interaction (a guarded `default` never discharges the `default` requirement) should land with or after S2e. S2e landed (2026-08-08) with coverage recording in MatchCase and the analysis in MatchStatement, so the check-side hook points exist; when this lands, a guarded `default` must record nothing into Context::MatchStatementContext, exactly like a guarded `case`. STATUS (updated 2026-08-18 by the W-067 implementer): DISCHARGED (confirmed 2026-08-18 by the coordinator: autoupdate fixpoint runs 32110931780/32111055736 + review-round 32112294566/32121167408; gate GREEN on re-fire 32121303702 after the 07:33Z runner-outage red 32111182653; conformance run 32111182558 landed the floor at EXACTLY 92 PASS / 0 FAIL / 29 SKIP over 121 with control_flow/match_guarded_default.carbon PASS — every staged condition met). PRIOR STAGING TEXT: DISCHARGE-STAGED under the R9 hedge. Landed content: parse gives `default` the optional guard production mirroring the case guard (shared HandleMatchGuard helper in parse/handle_match.cpp; new label node kind `MatchGuardedDefault` bracketed by MatchDefaultIntroducer with the existing MatchCaseGuard subtree as its second child; new state MatchGuardedDefaultStart), and — per the design's usefulness rule (a guard on any prior pattern is assumed able to evaluate to false, pattern_matching.md "Refutability, overlap, usefulness, and exhaustiveness", plus its "prior `default`" wording) — arms AFTER a guarded `default` are reachable and accepted (one-token `default`+`if` lookahead keeps MatchCaseLoop open; only an unguarded `default` ends the arm list and keeps the UnreachableMatchCase diagnostic). Check reuses the S2d capture-splice-branch shape with no pattern test and no bindings (constant-true test entering the arm, spliced guard region, guard-failure edge discharging the arm scope's cleanups and falling through to the next arm — the guarded-irrefutable-arm CFG minus NameBindingDecl), and the EXHAUSTIVENESS INTERACTION is as this entry required: a guarded `default` records NOTHING into MatchStatementContext and does not pop as MatchDefault, so it never discharges the `default` requirement; a guarded `default` followed by nothing is diagnosed by the EXISTING mandatory-default machinery unchanged (integer scrutinee: the SemanticsTodo no-default gate; choice scrutinee: MatchNonexhaustive naming the uncovered alternatives) — the design is silent on the dangling-else shape, so the reuse-not-mint diagnosis path was chosen per R6 and recorded in the decision-log landing note. Testdata: parse guarded_default.carbon + fail_missing_default_guard_{open,close}_paren.carbon; check guarded_default.carbon (basic chain with arms after the guarded default, compound `and` guard, choice coverage ACROSS a guarded default) + fail_guarded_default.carbon (integer TODO pin, choice-uncovered pin, non-bool guard conversion pin); conformance control_flow/match_guarded_default.carbon (runtime guard-true takes the default arm, guard-false falls through to a later case and the final unguarded default; RuntimeSeed x+20 inputs). DISCHARGES WHEN: the landing runner autoupdate reconciles the new goldens at R26 fixpoint (positive files ship with empty CHECK lines per R15/R19 — red-first is expected), the gate runs green, and the conformance floor moves to EXACTLY 92 PASS / 0 FAIL / 29 SKIP over 121 with the movement being ONLY match_guarded_default.carbon's PASS; any other movement re-opens this item with the run's evidence.

items.notes: Recorded at W5-S1 ('S2's exhaustiveness work is the natural place to admit them') and explicitly NOT discharged at S2e: plan §3.5 sanctions only the MatchStatement exhaustiveness analysis, and these choices have an empty-tuple discriminant — GetChoiceDiscriminantType requires an integer discriminant, so they fail the MatchCondition scrutinee gate (`match on unsupported scrutinee type`). Admitting them is scrutinee-gate + dispatch work, not coverage arithmetic: a single-alternative choice needs an always-taken arm with no discriminant test (constant-true condition, payload extraction still real for a payload alternative), and an empty choice needs a vacuously-exhaustive zero-arm match [scope amended at W-068: the zero-arm grammar half was cut by the lane-(b) decision — see the landing note; type admission + vacuous exhaustiveness through existing arms is what this item now claims] (parse currently requires at least one case or `default`). The S2e coverage machinery (Context::MatchStatementContext) already handles the exhaustiveness half once the gate admits them. W5-S3a's specifics-as-scrutinees lift composes with this gate rather than widening it: single-alternative and empty SPECIFICS of generic choices (Always(i32), Never(i32)) still fail the integer-discriminant check and keep the scrutinee TODO, pinned by choice_generic_scrutinee.carbon's fail_todo_single_alternative_specific and fail_todo_empty_choice_specific subfiles; discharging this item must flip those pins too [obligation SATISFIED at the W-068 slice: both subfiles flipped positive — single_alternative_specific + empty_choice_specific]. PRIOR STAGING TEXT: DISCHARGE-STAGED under the R9 hedge. Landed content: the scrutinee gate, alternative-pattern gate, and MatchStatement exhaustiveness split now ask the new IsMatchableChoiceType (pattern_match.cpp) — the same F-007k repr walk as GetChoiceDiscriminantType, factored into a shared GetChoiceDiscriminantFieldType, accepting an integer OR empty-tuple discriminant field (any other field type still fails safe, and the all-payloads-rejected error repr still degrades at the gate). Dispatch: where no integer discriminant exists, the alternative arm's condition is a constant true (MakeBoolLiteral — the W-067 guarded-default/binding-arm shape) in both the payload-arm path (MatchCaseAlternativePatternMatch) and the designator ExprPattern path (DoMatchCaseExprPattern); payload extraction is unchanged and real (GetChoicePayloadInfo never required the integer discriminant). Coverage needs NO arithmetic change: a single alternative is covered by its one unguarded arm, and an empty choice's empty alternative table leaves nothing missing — the DiagnoseNonexhaustiveMatch empty-table bail is now documented as also being the legitimate vacuous-exhaustiveness answer. EMPTY-CHOICE LANE (recorded decision): scrutinee-TYPE admission with parse's at-least-one-arm requirement kept — the zero-arm spelling `match (e) {}` stays a parse error (ExpectedMatchCases, parse/handle_match.cpp), because the design docs define exhaustiveness over pattern sets but give no zero-arm grammar, and empty-choice VALUES are unconstructible anyway (handle_choice.cpp gives an empty choice no constructors — 'there's no way to construct the Choice'), so a zero-arm body would be unreachable syntax; vacuous exhaustiveness IS real through the existing analysis (a guarded-`default`-only match over an empty choice compiles with no unguarded `default`, pinned by empty_choice.carbon's guarded_default_vacuous subfile). The zero-arm grammar is a language-design question, deliberately NOT minted as a fork work item (R17). Construction side verified: single-alternative construction (constant and payload alternatives, concrete and generic) landed at W5-S1/F-A1 and S3b (choice/single_payload_alternative.carbon check+lower); only empty-choice values are uninhabitable. items.notes: Surfaced by W5-S3b: once the generic-choice constructor rework made plib's `let g: P(i64) = P(i64).Neither;` check successfully, the importing file's `match (g)` crashed in lowering (function_context.cpp:190 — ImportRefLoaded with non-concrete value 'runtime'). This is not a choice bug: upstream has no cross-file runtime-global story for `let` at all — a `let` has no VarStorage, a class-typed `let` binds its value through a runtime temporary even when the initializer is constant, and the importer has no path that routes an ImportRefLoaded of a `let` binding to the defining file's backing storage the way `var` routes through the exported VarStorage global. The R-2 counter-program split was kept by moving the binding into the importing file as a local `let g` (imported_global) rather than silently dropping the cross-file scrutinee coverage [corrected at the W-069 plan round: this sentence previously said 're-authored to `var g`' — the interim var re-author was structurally wrong (a `var` initializes by copying, and choice types implement no Core.Copy) and was reverted within W5-S3b itself (commit ac1afa4); the tree's final S3b state is the local `let`, matching the subfile's own comment]; restoring a `let`-based split is the acceptance test for discharging this item. Half (b) of the fix landed with the W5-S3b import-crash round (import_ref.cpp, TryResolveInstCanonical's non-constant-binding branch): an imported binding whose BOUND VALUE is constant now resolves to that value's constant — translated with its generic attachment intact — so constant-bound `let`s and choice-alternative wrapper bindings import as constants and lower through the constant path. The residual gap is (a): a `let` bound to a RUNTIME value still has no exported backing storage (the materialized temporary would need promotion to a named global, referenced cross-file like VarStorage). Restoring a runtime-`let`-based cross-file split is the acceptance test for the residue. W69a progress (2026-08-18, STAGED under the R9 hedge — no discharge language until W69b's landing scoreboard): the scalar half of lane (a1) is implemented in toolchain/lower per fork/w069/plan.md §4 — a PrepareToLower pre-pass registers package-scope VALUE bindings whose bound value is NotConstant (the ExprCategory::Value test excludes `let ref`; class-scope statics stay out of scope per the plan's N-4 note); IsCopyOfObjectRepr shapes are promoted to named globals mangled by the new Mangler::MangleGlobalLetBinding (fingerprint input = the binding inst per the NIT-2 amendment); `__global_init` stores each bound value immediately after its ctor-resident initializer lowers (with a post-ctor unvisited-entry check); GetValue serves references — same-file cross-function and imported, with SemIR::GetCanonicalFileAndInstId chasing import/re-export chains per the SF-1 amendment — by loading from the global; ValueRepr None mints no storage; pointer/custom reps are Declined and fail loudly with a named W-069 message (W69b's arm). Goldens staged (autoupdate fills at the runner): check+lower testdata/let/global_runtime.carbon (P-1/P-2 incl. the export-import A/B/main subfile, P-7, P-8, P-9), lower testdata/let/global_runtime_symbols.carbon (the R-1 falsifier: defining file + two importers + private let), and the lower/testdata/var/import.carbon P-6 TODO flip (`fn X` added, :47 TODO removed; regeneration rides autoupdate per R16a). One recorded plan deviation for adjudication: the SF-1 golden's `export x;` (ExportDecl) re-export form cannot check today — import_ref.cpp:4483's non-constant branch CHECKs Is<AnyBinding> and an ExportDecl of a runtime let is not one — so the staged subfile uses the `export import` form; the ExportDecl arm of the lowering chase is implemented but golden-pinned only for the import-chain hops (see the decision-log W69a note; import_ref.cpp stays untouched per §5 step 3(ii)). items.notes: Recorded at the B2a conformance round (2026-08-09). SCOPE: values whose type is an associated-constant projection on a SYMBOLIC specific (`MyResult(T, i32).(Core.Try.ContinueType)`) are not reduced by the resolved forall impl's `where` rewrites (`.ContinueType = T`), so they cannot be bound `: T`, passed where `T` is expected, or wrapped by `Ok(v: T)` — generic `?` continue values are consumable ONLY via deduced sinks or projection-annotated bindings. Facet-BINDING rewrites do reduce (`R: Core.Try where .BreakType = i32` makes `R.FromBreak(0)` check — the W-071 discharge body), so the gap is specifically projections on specifics resolved through impl lookup rather than through a constrained binding. CONSEQUENCE for conformance: runtime arbitration of continue-value THREADING through a generic `?` chain is deferred on this item (question_generic_diff arbitrates the break path + per-instantiation layout roundtrip honestly). ADJACENT design residue for the B2b/SF-9 brief: `Core.Try` has no success constructor (Rust's `Try::from_output` analogue), so a facet-generic function cannot reconstruct its result type's Ok case — even with rewrite-reduction landed, fully generic Result-transformers need that interface surface. Today a `bool` scrutinee stays behind the scrutinee gate (`match on unsupported scrutinee type`, handle_match.cpp:238), pinned by fail_todo_non_int_scrutinee.carbon's bool-scrutinee probe. Implementation rides landed machinery: admit `bool` at the gate, compare via the expression-pattern `==` lane — which requires a deliberate, recorded widening of the R9 constant-integer admission to bool constants (pattern_match.cpp:1170) — and record `true`/`false` coverage the way choice alternatives record (S2e). Interaction: if W-066 lands first, its usefulness domain should include bool constant values from the start. DISCHARGED (2026-09-26, fork/w076/plan.md, full R11 loop; both plan reviews and both implementation reviews converged/approved — the plan reviews' shared major, the positionally-global R9 widening unlocking bool constants in choice-payload positions, was folded and pinned). items.notes: Filed at UN-1 discharge (fork/unions/plan.md §8.5). The design promises that a read whose bytes are not a valid value of the read type is 'not undefined behavior' and yields an unspecified value; UN-1's lowering is a plain typed load from the `[N x i8]` storage, and LLVM yields poison for, e.g., an `i1` load of a byte holding 2 — poison that becomes UB only if it propagates into a branch or a memory access. 0.1 therefore delivers the design's outcome only where the poison does not propagate. Not pinned: a golden cannot observe poison. Owning this item means either (a) a freeze on loads from union storage of types with invalid representations (`bool`, pointers with alignment assumptions, `choice` discriminants) — a lowering-only change, or (b) the F-007g debug-mode active-member tracking that turns such reads into a fail-stop, which is design work (a per-object shadow discriminant changes layout and must be opt-in). Decide (a) for 0.1 unless the design page is amended first.

items.notes: Filed at UN-1 discharge. The copyable half of the 0.1 field predicate (D-UN-2) is evaluated exactly once, when the union completes at its `}`, by enumerating the impls in the local store and the imported stores. Import-materialized impls are order-independent by rev 2b B-1 (skipped in the local leg, classified by their defining file), but a FILE-DECLARED user impl is visible only if it precedes the union textually: `class Counted { var n: i32; } union U { var c: Counted; } impl Counted as Core.Copy { ... }` admits `c` and the union's D-UN-5 byte copy then bypasses the user `Op` — the same program with the impl moved above the union diagnoses `UnionFieldNotTriviallyCopyable`. Not pinned (a failing pin would document a soundness hole rather than a diagnostic). Mechanisms, for the item to choose: (a) diagnose at the impl declaration — an `impl ... as Core.Copy` whose self class is already a field of a completed union (needs a class-to-unions reverse index, or a re-walk of `classes()` at `impl` completion); (b) re-run the copyable half lazily at the union's first copy (the `LookupChoiceCopyWitness` gate site), which catches the bypass but moves the diagnostic away from the field; (c) a design rule that a user `Copy` impl must precede any union naming the class as a field. Note that the destructible half has the same shape (`HasUserDestroyImpl` enumerates the store at completion) and the same fix applies.

items.notes: Filed at UN-1 discharge. D-UN-2 deliberately did NOT copy `HasUserDestroyImpl`'s symbolic-self shortcut ('any symbolic-self impl in scope disqualifies every class') into the copyable half, because the prelude declares blanket `Core.Copy` impls over `T*`, `const T`, `Int(N)`, `Optional(T)`; the landed walk instead matches an impl only when its self constant is a `ClassType` of the field's class (concrete, or symbolic of the same class_id, which covers `impl forall [T] MyBox(T) as Copy`). Consequently a USER blanket impl declared outside package `Core` with a non-class self — `impl forall [T: type] T as Core.Copy`, or `impl forall [T: type] T* as Core.Copy` for a pointer field — is neither matched nor rejected: a field whose `Core.Copy` lookup would resolve to it is admitted and the union's D-UN-5 byte copy bypasses it. Unpinned (same reason as W-092). Mechanism: in the user-package legs ONLY (local store when `package_id() != Core`; imported stores whose package is not `Core`), a `Core.Copy` impl whose self constant is symbolic and not a `ClassType` counts as a user impl for every field — the `HasUserDestroyImpl` shortcut restricted to the trust boundary's outside — plus a pointer/scalar arm that checks the same set. The prelude's impls stay trusted, so `i32`, `T*` and `Optional(T*)` fields keep passing (the `optional_pointer_field` pin). Fix in the same change as W-092 if possible; they share the helper.

Checked-generic calls resolve ONCE at the definition against symbolic types (D-OV-4 step 7: a symbolic conversion either resolves through a constraint or fails; there is no "depends on the specific" case). A template-dependent argument cannot be probed at the definition: its type is unknown until substitution, so the call diagnoses the TODO and returns `ErrorInst`. Mechanism: resolve after substitution — defer the call as a deferred action the way template-dependent member access is deferred today (the `template T: type` machinery of "Generics: Integrated templates", itself PARTIAL), re-running `PerformCallToOverloadSet` on the substituted argument types per specific; the stranded page's "Calls from template code" section describes the semantics. The candidate probe deduces a generic member non-diagnosing INSIDE the discard scope, but deduction ends in `MakeSpecific`, which runs `ResolveSpecificDecl` — the generic's declaration block is evaluated in the minted specific before the conversion loop decides whether the member is selected. For a candidate that deduction accepts and conversion rejects (the `discard_probe_constants` shape), `specifics()` keeps the specific (predicted and pinned as the extra `define`) and any diagnostic that evaluating the declaration block emits — an `impls`/`where` requirement on a parameter type failing for the deduced arguments — is emitted for a candidate the call never selects. Mechanism: deduce without minting (split `DeduceGenericCallArguments` so the probe gets the deduced argument block and the commit mints), or mint under a suppressed emitter (the W-028 probe subsystem). items.notes: Filed at OV-3 discharge (fork/overload/plan.md §8.5; the implementation review's MINOR 6; id allocated after SL-1's W-108..W-116, final at the trunk merge). The Carbon-to-C++ type map is injective for the realistic cases — on LP64 `Cpp.long` IS `i64`, so that pair is a Carbon redeclaration error; return-type-only differences are rejected on the Carbon side — but naming `Core.CppCompat.Long64` explicitly beside `i64`, or `Core.Char` beside the char-literal type, yields two members whose C++ declarations have one signature. Outcome is Clang's "call to 'F' is ambiguous" at every C++ call of the set, not a crash or a duplicate-symbol error (the internal-linkage inline `F`s are emitted only when selected, and an ambiguous call selects neither); the Carbon side is unaffected. Unpinned: no golden names `Core.CppCompat.Long64` in a set. Mechanism: an `ASTContext::hasSameType` compare of each new member decl's type against the list before `push_back`, dropping the later member with a semantics TODO (or a dedicated note) naming the earlier.

items.notes: Filed at UA-1 fill round 3 (the round 2 review's F2 and F3). The guard decides per TYPE: classes are always pointer-represented, structs and tuples with two or more elements too, symbolic types are dependent, so `fn F(c: bool, arr: array((i32, i32), 2)) -> (i32, i32) { return if c then arr[Make(1).x] else arr[0]; }` is rejected although the value is backed by `arr`, not by the `Make(1)` temporary the arm destroys (upstream cannot compile it in fastbuild either: the temporary's destroy in `if.expr.result` trips PR 7771's SSA verifier). False negatives: none found -- copy-represented values are loaded by `acquire_value` before the arm's destroy, `None` has no value. Corpus impact today: none (every `if`-expression arm in check/lower testdata, examples/advent2024 and the conformance programs is an `i32`, `bool`, pointer, type constant or var reference; a short-circuit right operand is `bool` by construction). Language-surface cost (F3): class-valued arms with a materialized temporary -- `if c then Make(1) else Make(2)`, `(if c then Open(n) else Open(m))?`, `F(if c then MakeC() else MakeC2())` -- are a hard TODO; before the merge the fork compiled them and miscompiled the non-trivial-destructor case (the other arm's unconstructed temporary was destroyed in `if.expr.result`), and no upstream-accepted program is lost. items.notes: Filed by the SC-1 commit-3 fixer (2026-10-12) as W-144, id allocated above W-143 under the same cross-branch assumption as W-134..W-143 (origin/trunk W-125, origin/claude/carbon-fork-0-1-ua2 W-126/W-127, origin/claude/carbon-fork-0-1-cmake W-128..W-133, origin/claude/carbon-fork-0-1-safe none above W-125; verified at merge); renumbered from W-144 on 2026-10-13 because SAFE-1 (PR 53, origin/claude/carbon-fork-0-1-safe) allocated W-144..W-150, so this is the next free id above every branch. The look-through's two shape checks (object member versus `self` presence; explicit parameter count) narrow the exposure but do not close it: a one-candidate `Get` of the right arity whose parameter or return type the importer cannot map, or whose fenced thunk cannot be built, emits during the silent member-1 probe of `overload fn Pick[template T: HasGet](p: T*)` / `[template T: type]`, so the program is COMPILE-FAIL instead of selecting member 2 -- the same class as the commit-2 review's finding 3 (the compound redirect's unconditional diagnostics), reachable only through the interop look-through. Deliberately NOT fixed by gating the import on `diagnose`: the conformance programs' member-1 probe is itself a `diagnose = false` path and must import for a C++ class to satisfy at all. Mechanism: thread `diagnose` into `ImportCppDecl` / `ImportCppFunctionDecl` (check/cpp/, untouched by SC-1 per fork/structural/plan.md §2.C) so the import's TODOs are suppressed in check mode and a failed import reads as a mismatch, with the explain-mode re-run emitting them; the split then loses its `fail_todo_` prefix.

items.notes: Filed at the ST-1 discharge (2026-10-13, fork/string/plan.md §1.3, §1.7, D-ST-7, D-ST-16). Under the classes bullet, not the String bullet, because the mechanism leaks for every class with a `Destroy`, `Core.Buf` included (plan review B's B3). The design rewrites `=` to `AssignWith`; the toolchain initializes the left operand in place without destroying its old value, so the overwritten block leaks (never a double free). ST-1's documented API never assigns a `Core.StringBuf`: loops append with `+=`, and no program, golden or doc example shows `s = s + t`. Mechanism: build the destroy of the old value before the right-hand side (the TODO's own plan), or route `=` through `AssignWith`. Break condition: assigning a `Core.StringBuf` twice frees both overwritten blocks under the plan's §8.8 shim.

items.notes: DISCHARGED (fork/optional2/plan.md OP-2, 2026-10-14; branch claude/carbon-fork-0-1-op2, stacked on PR 56's head 379f20f67; plan commits 963adda99 rev 1, 4027885b3 rev 2 and a5b81889b rev 3 with the sign-off; 757cd0e74 the toolchain, the prelude and the CHECK-free goldens, 189baa262 the autoupdate fill, 503d25895 the programs, the docs and the row, 9f9ccd768 and f859c7e73 the implementation-review fold, c396efeae the merge of trunk f67ab650d, then the discharge commit; decision-log "OP-2 / F-016: Core.Optional ownership, adapter destruction, the MaybeUnformed representation fix, checked Get"). What landed (fork/optional2/plan.md §1.2): destroying a non-empty `Core.Optional(T)` destroys its value once, through the default storage's declared `Destroy` (D-OP2-4), which is reached because an adapter is now destroyed as its adapted type (D-OP2-3, fork design F-016, minted at this discharge), while `Core.Optional(T*)` stays trivially destructible, a union may still hold one and its C++ pointer ABI is unchanged; a checked generic can create and destroy a `Core.Optional(T)` because `OptionalStorage.Type` is `Destroy` (D-OP2-5, M-8); copying is unchanged and each copy is destroyed once (M-9). Root cause, measured: the toolchain treated every adapter as trivially destructible (`Class::GetStructTypeFields` returns no fields for an adapter), so a storage `Destroy` alone changed nothing (M-5: `2 1 1 0 3 2`); the same defect is upstream's (trunk d4f1ec203's custom_witness.cpp :276-279) and dropped the destruction of any adapter of a type with destruction work (adapter_destroy.carbon `0 201` before, `0 202 201` after). Corrections of plan §0.3 items 2 and 3: the notes and OP-1's D-OP-12 said a declared `Destroy` makes every Optional, the pointer niche included, user-destructible, which is true of an impl keyed on `Optional` and not of one on the default storage, which never reaches `Optional(T*)` (M-6); and the subsystem, written "core/prelude (+ the union field rule)", is "core/prelude + toolchain/check (custom_witness.cpp)", because the root cause is also in the toolchain. The break condition as OP-1 wrote it: "a `Destroy` for `Core.Optional` that keeps `Core.Optional(T*)` trivially destructible lands with no union or interop regression, and optional_destroys_value un-SKIPs to PASS in a conformance run of record"; as D-OP2-6 amends it: "a `Destroy` for `Core.Optional` that keeps `Core.Optional(T*)` trivially destructible lands with no regression of a `Core.Optional(T*)` union field or of the C++ pointer mapping, and optional_destroys_value un-SKIPs to PASS in a conformance run of record (D-OP2-16)". Met as amended: `Core.Optional(i32*)` and `Core.Optional(C*)` union fields compile (union/basic, the `union_pointer_field` split), no interop golden gains a diagnostic and a `Core.Optional(i32*)` class field still maps to C++ (M-22), and optional_destroys_value PASSes. The one union regression, a `Core.Optional(i32)` field now `UnionFieldNotTriviallyCopyable`, is D-OP2-6's accepted consequence, pinned by `fail_union_value_field` and filed as W-196. The conformance run of record its break condition names is satisfied, by D-OP2-16 while Actions is disabled, by the plan's §8.8 container run, stated EXPECTED, not of record: on the merge of trunk c396efeae with the carbonbuild toolchain of 9f9ccd768, whose toolchain and prelude that merge does not change (`carbon version` 0.0.0-0.dev+9f9ccd768), scoreboard generated 2026-10-14T05:49:31Z, PASS 139, COMPILE-FAIL 0, LINK-FAIL 0, RUN-FAIL 0, OUTPUT-MISMATCH 0, DIFF-MISMATCH 0, SKIP 22 over 161, bullets 48 PASS / 0 FAIL / 8 SKIP of 56, with exactly the plan's seven status changes from PR 56's container run (132/0/25 over 157); file_test 1950 passed, 0 failed on the same tree; the hosted run of record is pending (Actions disabled). D-OP2-16's break condition: if the §8.8 run at the land-time merge of trunk or the first hosted run of record shows optional_destroys_value, optional_destroy_diff or optional_cpp_class_destroy not PASS, this item is re-opened with that run and the row 'Stdlib: Optional' reverts to PARTIAL in the next commit. Residues: W-196 (a non-pointer Optional is not trivially destructible), W-197 (a class with its own `Destroy` does not destroy an Optional field; filed because PR 51, whose W-126 is the same defect, is not on trunk), W-199 (`Core.Optional(const C)` keeps its value, as any `const C` object does), W-200 (only `Core.Optional(T*)` may be declared without an initializer). History: Filed at the OP-1 discharge (2026-10-13, fork/optional/plan.md §1.3, §1.7, D-OP-12, D-OP-13). Row-bounding: one of the two items that keep the `Stdlib: Optional` row PARTIAL (D-OP-13). F-015's rule is that an Optional owns its value and destroying a non-empty Optional destroys it, as C++ `std::optional`, Rust `Option` and p001154:211-227's considered sketch do; the 0.1 toolchain does not, because the default storage's `MaybeUnformed(T)` runs no destructor. The destroy must stay trivial for the pointer niche (unions.md:233-239, p006357:247-249). Design inputs: classes.md:1992-2003 (a class that defines a destructor with a non-empty body is not `TrivialDestructor`, :1995-1996) and p001154:211-227 (the considered conditional `TrivialDestructor` `Optional` sketch). Consequences measured by the implementation review: in a checked generic `[T: Core.Eq & Core.Copy & Core.Destroy]`, `Core.Optional(T).Some(a).HasValue()`, `Mk(a) == b` with `Mk` returning `Core.Optional(T)`, and `let o: Core.Optional(T) = ...; o == b` each fail with "cannot access member of interface `Core.Destroy` in type `Core.Optional(T as Core.OptionalStorage)` that does not implement that interface" (trunk too), so generic code compares only Optionals it receives; `o1 == o2` on two `Core.Optional(Core.Optional(P))` values holding P1 and P2 printed, before W-352, `101 102 101 102 202 201 0`, four `P` copies and two destroys, leaking one `P` per operand; since OP-1's in-place comparison (W-352, c655d55f3) it copies and destroys nothing (trace `0`); on M-6's prototype the three generic forms check and the trace balances (`101 102 101 102 202 201 202 201 0`). Break condition: a `Destroy` for `Core.Optional` that keeps `Core.Optional(T*)` trivially destructible lands with no union or interop regression, and optional_destroys_value un-SKIPs to PASS in a conformance run of record. (LAND-1, 2026-11-05: the "not of record" label above is superseded by PR 57's landing's container-measured scoreboard, R33 (b), 208/0/14 over 222 with 50/56 bullets.)

Fixed at its root in lowering (D-OP2-1): compatible types share an object representation but not necessarily a value representation (`MaybeUnformed(T)` takes a pointer where `T` may take a copy, check/type_completion.cpp), and in a generic only the specific being lowered knows which; `GetValueRepr` adds the kinds to the specific's fingerprint, so the `bool`, `i32` and `Core.Optional(i32*)` specifics of one generic are never coalesced. The check-side round trip stays with its CHECK testing the operand (D-OP2-2). Corrections of plan §0.3 items 1 and 4: the notes said SC-1 moves the CHECK to convert.cpp:1712; it is :1701 on this branch (:1698 at 379f20f67, three fork comment lines above it), and on SC-1's head ee1f905b0 :1712, where the landed toolchain diff applies with offsets +14 (convert.cpp) and +2 (custom_witness.cpp) and handle.cpp unchanged (`git apply --check`, re-read at this discharge); and the title's "the default storage silently return[s] the storage address" misplaces the defect, which is not the storage's: any value `as_compatible` whose two types' representations differ was a no-op, concretely after adapter stripping (`m unsafe as Core.Optional(i32*)` printed `-366584636` for 7, M-2's mu_opt_run) and in every generic (M-2's `G`), and the concrete `MaybeUnformed(bool) unsafe as bool` failed the CHECK, which tested the target. Its initializer twin, an initializing `as_compatible` whose two init representations differ, is not fixed and is filed as W-198 (M-18); a single-element aggregate of a pointer-represented element, which the implementation review found reaching the new arms, now stops at `CheckCopyValueIsObject` and is filed as W-201 (trunk's defect). Both toolchain fixes repair upstream code (upstream trunk d4f1ec203 carries the same convert.cpp block, M-3; upstream PR 6334 introduced it); the plan's landed notes list the reproducers for an upstream report. The break condition as OP-1 wrote it: "`Get()`, copy and `==` lower correctly for both payloads, and optional_bool and optional_nested_pointer un-SKIP to PASS in a conformance run of record". Met: both PASS, `==` included. The conformance run of record its break condition names is satisfied, by D-OP2-16 while Actions is disabled, by the plan's §8.8 container run, stated EXPECTED, not of record: on the merge of trunk c396efeae with the carbonbuild toolchain of 9f9ccd768, whose toolchain and prelude that merge does not change (`carbon version` 0.0.0-0.dev+9f9ccd768), scoreboard generated 2026-10-14T05:49:31Z, PASS 139, COMPILE-FAIL 0, LINK-FAIL 0, RUN-FAIL 0, OUTPUT-MISMATCH 0, DIFF-MISMATCH 0, SKIP 22 over 161, bullets 48 PASS / 0 FAIL / 8 SKIP of 56, with exactly the plan's seven status changes from PR 56's container run (132/0/25 over 157); file_test 1950 passed, 0 failed on the same tree; the hosted run of record is pending (Actions disabled). History: Filed at the OP-1 discharge (2026-10-13, fork/optional/plan.md §1.2, §1.7, D-OP-13). Row-bounding (D-OP-13). With OP-1, `==` on `Core.Optional(bool)` reaches the same crash, where trunk and upstream give a check error (M-20). SC-1 moves the CHECK to convert.cpp:1712; re-read at the merge of trunk. The root cause, optional.carbon:169-171 and :172-178: for `tt: Core.Optional(Core.Optional(i32*))` the unoptimized IR of `*tt.Get().Get()` has the storage `Get` pass `getelementptr inbounds nuw <{ ptr, i1 }>, ptr %value, i32 0, i32 0` to the inner `Optional(i32*)` `Copy`, which is `ret ptr %self`, with no load. Break condition: R09 compiles and runs with the constraint consulted, X21's `x.F()` is rejected when `G` is instantiated, and the templates.md limit is removed. DISCHARGED by TP-1: on instantiation a member of a template-dependent operand is looked up in the argument type and in the parameter's constraint (member_access.cpp `PerformAction(AccessMemberAction)`); R09 runs (25), X21's `x.F()` is rejected with `TemplateMemberLookupAmbiguous`, and a field beside a constraint method is rejected too (constraint_lookup.carbon); templates.md's limit keeps its text with a dated resolution note (Appendix C of the plan). items.notes: Filed at the OP-2 discharge (2026-10-14, fork/optional2/plan.md §1.7, D-OP2-6). `Core.Optional(T)` for a non-pointer `T` is not trivially destructible, even when `T` is: its default storage defines a destructor with a non-empty body, which classes.md's rule makes not `TrivialDestructor`, and by F-016 the `Optional` adapter is trivially destructible exactly when its storage is. So a `Core.Optional(i32)` union field is rejected (`UnionFieldNotTriviallyCopyable`, M-7), and destroying one tests `has_value` and calls the payload's out-of-line `SelfDestruct`, a no-op for `i32` that the optimizer cannot remove (M-10, M-20). C++ export is not affected: a Carbon class with a `Core.Optional(i32)` field does not map to C++ before or after OP-2 (W-049, M-22). C++'s `std::optional<T>` is trivially destructible exactly when `T` is ([optional.dtor]); p001154:211-227's conditional `TrivialDestructor` is the considered alternative, and classes.md's rule with F-016 the adopted rule that excludes it. Not row-bounding: no operation of `Core.Optional` fails, and no design statement admits a `Core.Optional(i32)` union field (unions.md admits `Core.Optional(T*)` fields only). Break condition: an accepted design adopts conditional `TrivialDestructor`, and `Core.Optional(i32)` is then trivially destructible and a union field again; or a measured program needs it sooner, and the plan's §7 A-11 scalar storage is the interim fix.

items.notes: Filed at the OP-2 discharge (2026-10-14, fork/optional2/plan.md §1.7, D-OP2-15; plan review A's A-1; implementation review R1-m1). A non-pointer `Core.Optional` cannot be declared without an initializer (`var o: Core.Optional(i32);` is `ConversionFailureTypeToFacet` into `Core.DefaultOrUnformed`), because the default storage's `Destroy` reads `has_value` and an unformed object leaves it uninitialized; only `Core.Optional(T*)` is `UnformedInit` (D-OP2-15, which amends F-015's API, docs/design/optional.md's `UnformedInit` row). The same hazard returns through a user `UnformedInit` impl on a class holding, or an adapter of, a non-pointer `Core.Optional` (d3, d4): such an impl breaks `UnformedInit`'s contract that destroying an unformed object is valid (core/prelude/default.carbon:15-17), as one on a class with a `Core.Buf` field would, and the toolchain does not prevent it; optional.md's W-200 limit and the classes.md F-016 amendment say so. Proposal p000257 expects an `Optional(T)` to give any payload an unformed state represented as the empty value (:193-220, :333-340), which needs `UnformedInit` to initialize a field (default.carbon:19-24's TODO). Not row-bounding: no design rule requires an unformed state of the 0.1 Optional (D-OP2-12). Break condition: an unformed-state-aware destroy lands (W-115's mechanism), or `UnformedInit` can initialize `has_value` to false; then `impl forall [T: OptionalStorage & UnformedInit] Optional(T) as UnformedInit {}` is restored with the `fail_unformed_value` split made positive.

items.notes: Filed by the SC-1 fill-round-15 fixer (2026-10-14) under SC-1's reservation W-238..W-239, as round 14's review 1 asked (MAJOR-1's fix (1), W-234's precedent) and review 2 asked (MINOR-1's fix, the refusal its optional second step). Before fill round 15 every build since the structural check called `CheckFunctionTypeMatches` aborted on a requirement with an expression pattern parameter that has no error against a member with one: such a pattern's type is not the error, so the errors-match mode does not take the pair, and upstream's switch reaches its default. 55d77c5e1's subject ("an expression-pattern requirement no longer aborts") held only for a requirement in the same file whose expression pattern has an error, and D-SC-9's maintenance note said an unlisted kind is not aborted on (both scoped at fill round 15). The refusal keeps a TODO of its own, beside the expression pattern's, so that such a requirement is never dropped silently once upstream accepts expression patterns in parameter lists. The import aborts are upstream's: `TryResolveInstCanonical` resolves the parameter patterns of an imported function, and of the functions of an imported interface or template constraint when it is named, and has no case for `ExprPattern`; patching it would change import for every caller, so SC-1 leaves it, and no program reaching it is valid, since the expression pattern's TODO is diagnosed in the same invocation. Break condition: upstream implements expression patterns in parameter lists (`CheckRedeclParam` and `TryResolveInstCanonical` handle `ExprPattern`, and the "expression pattern" TODO goes); then the refusal goes, such a requirement is collected, and the split becomes positive. Amended at fill round 16 (round 15's two reviews): `GetDeclaredParamPattern` imported the subpattern of an imported pattern whose constant value is the error, so a member imported with `var z` or `(z) = 1` aborted every use against a template constraint, a path of SC-1's own that no trunk analog shares (review 2's MAJOR-1); such a subpattern is now compared by its kind without being imported, the wrapping pattern keeping its kind so that each imported case gives its local twin's result, and that guard goes with the `TryResolveInstCanonical` case named above. The title's import aborts are now upstream's alone: naming an imported template constraint with such a requirement, and looking up an imported member whose parameter is such a pattern directly or under `var 1 = Undefined`. A refused requirement is not checked at all, so the `var y` shape is silent at a use where trunk's impl analog reports through the thunk (review 1's MINOR-1), and a redeclaration of such a requirement inside the constraint aborts in upstream's redeclaration merge before the refusal runs (review 1's MINOR-3); both are recorded in the evidence, and neither changes a toolchain file. Amended at fill round 17 (round 16's two reviews): the round-16 guard skipped an `ExprPattern` subpattern only, so a member imported with a default value with an error on a tuple pattern that holds one (`(1, w: i32) = Undefined`) still aborted every use inside SC-1's comparison (both reviews' MAJOR-1); a `TuplePattern` subpattern is not imported either now, the other kind that no requirement has, compared by its kind alone so that each such imported case gives its local twin's result, and that guard goes with the same `TryResolveInstCanonical` case. The title's upstream-shared import aborts are worded to their measured scope, an error-free expression pattern anywhere upstream's function import walks, `var 1 = Undefined` among them (review 1's MINOR-2, review 2's MINOR-2); no toolchain file changes for that. Amended at fill round 18 (round 17's two reviews, records only): the title names the refusal under a default value, which `GetRefusedParamPatternKind` has walked for an expression pattern since fill round 15 (review 2's MINOR-2); the evidence states that a `var` pattern beneath a default value with an error does not stop upstream's import walk (review 1's MINOR-1) and places a generic class's import abort at the class's name lookup (review 1's MINOR-2); no toolchain file changes.

Removal needs the import of action and splice instructions and a representation of an imported template's instantiation in check and lowering. Break condition: a use of a template from another library must compile and run (W-014's second arbiter clause). Amended 2026-10-15 (focused re-review of the fold: RR1-M1 / RR2-M1 / RR1-m2): the title names what the test detects, an eval block that holds an action or a splice, and covers class templates' field types and member function declarations and interfaces and named constraints. Amended 2026-10-15 (focused re-review of the fold, round 2: RR2r2-M1 / RR2r2-m1): the test walks what the entity's loaded data names, so no error constant reaches an eval block or a binding's type in any shape the two rounds measured; `HasErrorConstraint` is reached by a parameter of such a facet type in a function that is not generic (`fail_todo_import_function_parameter_of_template_interface_type`). Amended 2026-10-15 (focused re-review of the fold, round 3: RR3-1-M1 / RR3r2-M1 / RR3r2-m1): round 2's walk tested only the kind of each entry it reached, so a template named through a concrete operand of an entry (a callee, a specific's argument, a tuple or struct element, a field type beside one of type `T`, a constraint's argument or rewrite, a blanket impl's witness) still put an error constant in an eval block after the TODO, and a checked generic that calls a template whose definition alone holds an action imported that specific's definition; the walk now follows each reference that the import loads, and no error constant reaches an eval block or a binding's type in the 110 cross-library probes of round 3.
