items.notes: Filed at round 4 of the focused re-review of TP-1's fold (2026-10-15, fork/templates/plan.md §1.13 item 23). Before round 4 the fork stopped lowering x02, x18 and x20 at function_context.cpp:264's missing-value CHECK (RR4-1-B1) and rejected y03 where the function is defined (`ArrayInitDependentBound`); round 4's deferral (c841ad9e7, 6aa403cd6) converts them on instantiation, where the fork now rejects them as trunk and the nightly do. A runtime literal is referred to through a `SpecificInst`, takes the default and reaches W-265, as without a template (x19). Removal: refer to a deferred literal as a literal, so that `get_default` applies on instantiation. Amended 2026-10-15 (focused re-review of the fold, round 5: RR5-1-M1 / RR5r2-M1 / RR5r2-m1): 6aa403cd6 also deferred the class value of a class whose fields hold no such part, so a constant literal of such a class was rejected the same way, outside this item's title (the round-5 reviews' e01, e03, e04, e13, e15, p01, p03, p05, p06, p09 and p10, which f3f99c1c1 compiled and ran); since 0bd0756c8 such a class value is converted where the function is defined and takes its defaults, so the rejection is limited to the title's classes again, and the two pins are named `fail_todo_` since aec81d0ee. The removal changes the operand that eval.cpp's `GetConstantValue` for a `MetaInstId` (eval.cpp:503-513) gives every action, which is an operand's constant value when it has one, so round 5 left it filed. Amended 2026-10-15 (focused re-review of the fold, round 6: RR6-1-M1 / RR6r2-M1): the item holds, whatever the class's fields hold, for a literal that omits a field whose default initializer splices in a template action of the class's generic, which 0bd0756c8 converted where the function is defined, where lowering stopped at function_context.cpp:264, and which 4d015cf18 defers (`omits_produced_default`), so that it is rejected on instantiation as on trunk; and for a constant literal that leaves a field to its default nested in a class value, an array value or an argument that is converted on instantiation whole, which predates round 5 and which no round changes. Both are this item's mechanism, and its removal removes both; converting a nested constant literal where the function is defined instead, as 0bd0756c8 does for one that is not nested, was not made, as a second workaround of the mechanism for one more shape. Break condition: x02 compiles and prints 9. The second review's a01 printing 5 is a second one. DISCHARGED at round 7 of the focused re-review of TP-1's fold (2026-10-15, RR7r2-M1; fork/templates/plan.md §1.13 item 23): eval.cpp's `GetConstantValue` for a `MetaInstId` keeps a struct or tuple literal as an action's operand instead of its constant value (c4d609c8d), which is this item's recorded removal, so a deferred constant literal is converted as a literal on instantiation and `get_default` gives the fields it omits the defaults of the class's concrete specific, nested literals included; x02 prints 9 and a01 prints 5, both break conditions, and the six pins succeed and are named without `fail_todo_`. Round 6's deferral had also covered a default that converts a constant to the class's template type parameter, `var k: T = 7;`, which every TP-1 head before 4d015cf18 ran (the round-7 second review's w01, 11), so until this fix the item held a form that TR-4 counted IN. A struct value formed another way, `({.a = 4} as {.a: i32})`, stays rejected with a missing field, as without a template.

items.notes: Filed at round 8 of the focused re-review of TP-1's fold (2026-10-15, fork/templates/plan.md §1.13 item 25). Not a TP-1 regression: trunk and the nightly stop the same way. A template action's conversion relies on the eval block's completion of its target class type, which is deferred while the type is symbolic, so `D(U)`'s definition is not resolved when the conversion reads its object representation; round 8 resolves it before a field default is read, which turns the same call for `var k: i32 = N + 1;` in `class D(template N: i32)` into a diagnostic, but here the object representation depends on `T` and is read first. A literal that names every field, `{.a = 4, .k = 7}`, is rejected with ``cannot implicitly convert ... to `U` `` on the branch, where trunk and the nightly stop too (x07). C++ overload resolution sees a Carbon sum value or `Core.Optional(T)` given as an initializing expression, such as `.Some(5)`, as an rvalue of its C++ class, so it binds a `T&&` parameter and prefers the `T&&` member of a `const T&`/`T&&` pair such as `std::vector::push_back`; the parameter's initialization is located at its C++ declaration, which gives the conversion's branches no parse node, so the conversion gives this TODO there. By value, `const&` and `const&&` parameters convert; a value (a `let` or parameter binding, a constant such as `.None`, or `as` the C++ class) is offered as an lvalue, selects the `const T&` member of a pair, and is refused by a lone `T&&` by C++'s rule, as a value of the C++ class is on trunk; a C++ call's result binds the `T&&`. Not bounding row 68: the row's arbiter is the consumption of C++ values by `match`, which this shape does not touch, and the other parameter forms convert. Removal: attribute the blocks to the argument's own parse node where the parameter's location is not one (mutant M22 of the plan runs the sum-type forms that way; the `Core.Optional` form needs the node of the value before its bridge). Break condition: that removal lands, or the conversion becomes one call to a synthesized function per specialization (plan §7.2 R-K).

items.notes: Filed 2026-10-21 at DR-0 (owner directive "Direction drifts are not permitted"; R32). Mechanism (D-DR-1 slice 1, option (a)): implement sum_types.md's `Match` interface for classes and give `Core.Optional` `impl as Match`; `.Some(<pattern>)` and `.None` patterns over it in `match`, `if let` and `while let`, and the `for` desugaring rewritten to upstream loops.md's `match` with `case .Some(<pattern>)`; the `Try` impl body rewritten to error_handling.md's `match` sketch, a new decision because D-EH-1's and D-OP-7's break conditions are keyed on a choice and do not fire. Kept: the class, the `T*` null niche (p006357's pointer ABI), `argv: Core.Optional(char*)*`, the `Try` signature, `HasValue`/`Get`. Cost: the mechanism W5 (R-8) and the match re-platform excluded; a `Continuation` per sum type, compiler-filled bodies, a second scrutinee path; no upstream code to copy (upstream's toolchain/check/handle_match.cpp:11-76 handlers are TODOs). Rejected alternatives (DR-0): a choice `Optional` (rejected on record by D-EH-1, D-OP-7 and PR 62's option (d)) and a toolchain special case lowering `.Some`/`.None` to `HasValue`/`Get` (a fork-local spelling, a drift under R32 (d)). Touches PR 56, PR 57, PR 62's view (W-322) and the match goldens. Closes PR 56's W-177 when it lands. Owner: DR-1 slice 1, scheduled after CT-1's implementation and before UA-3. Break condition: upstream lands an `Optional` proposal or prelude change that makes it a choice, or implements its `.Some(pattern_id)` TODO by another mechanism (switch to that spelling and re-plan SF-6 and the niche), or implements `Match` first (copy it). Stopped 2026-10-21 at DR-1's plan (fork/direction/plan.md rev 3, §1.4, D-DR-22): sum_types.md's `Match` needs a template associated constant, which upstream's README.md and generics/terminology.md rule out and its parser refuses, and implementing it would be a new drift (R32); W-324 watches upstream's resolution. items.notes: Filed 2026-10-26 at the weekly upstream check (upstream 21c825a3f), its reader's claim as corrected by its verifier. Provenance: F-009j (D-OV-4 step 2(b), OV-1, 2026-09-28) was true of OV-1's tree and became false when UA-1 brought upstream's positional default values on 2026-10-05; neither UA-1's audit nor the 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-19 weeklies named it (the 2026-09-21 weekly named upstream PR 7737 on default values). 503f09037 and 9799a2326 only extend defaults to generic functions and to C++ export. The call is diagnosed, not miscompiled (read from the code; no build this week): the defect is that an overload set rejects a call the plain path accepts. Mechanism: the arity step accepts from n minus `default_value_arity` to n explicit arguments, and `ProbeOverloadCandidateInScratchScope` probes only the supplied arguments against their parameter patterns (the commit already runs the plain path, which fills the defaulted tail); the comment at :420-423 is rewritten; goldens pin a defaulted member called with the argument omitted and supplied, and a set in which a default makes two members accept one call (first match wins, D-OV-4); functions_overloading.md:570-576 and :1022-1023 are rewritten to name upstream's default values. Generic overload members with defaults take 503f09037's deduce support at UA-3, whose audit re-checks this item. No held PR carries the drift (no held branch adds a no-default-arguments statement; PR 59's call.cpp keeps the exact range at :574-587), so no held PR is amended under R32 (e); PR 59's W-215 already treats default values beside a pack as a Carbon feature. Owner: OV-4, the overload workstream's default-value slice, on trunk's base, after VA-2 lands and before UA-3 (ORCHESTRATION Next actions item 6). Break condition: upstream's design picks a different optional-parameter mechanism (classes.md:2186-2205's candidates) or removes positional defaults; the item then follows that mechanism. Discharged 2026-10-28 by OV-4 (fork/overload/ov4-plan.md; decision-log entry OV-4): the filed mechanism was necessary but not sufficient, because D-OV-6 gate (iii) refused every defaulted member at its declaration, member identity treated a default as a different parameter (a declaration differing only in a default became a second member of the same parameter types), and a diagnosed non-trailing default left the plain path's arity open (the CHECKs at pattern_match.cpp:1275 and, when the unmatched parameter is a tuple pattern, :1805, on trunk and the nightly); OV-4 changed those three too, each at its root, with one resolution path and no new diagnostic. The filed notes' "functions_overloading.md:570-576 and :1022-1023 are rewritten" is done in place, each rewrite quoting the text it supersedes. Generic members with defaults wait for 503f09037 at UA-3 (W-360), exported members' C++ default arguments for 9799a2326, 8fdc8ebc3 and c7de72757 (W-361); the default count's fix moves into function.cpp at UA-3 (W-362). The implementation reviews found the set's copy of `ResolveCalleeInCall`'s arity CHECK reachable through a diagnosed implicit-list `self`; ef31d5820 gives such a member the empty range, and the ordinary call's abort there, upstream's, is W-363. items.notes: Filed 2026-11-03 by the orchestrator's ruling under R29 on FO-1 unit D's review 1 finding D-R1-m1 (fork/followon/fo1-plan.md, unit D's implementation record): a pre-existing defect of trunk's tuple lowering, not W-368's, filed in a records commit of its own outside FO-1's slices and landings. After W-368's fix (PR 59, D2: a pack laid out at its element's array stride) the check is shared by packs: a pack of one `Core.Int(24)` or `Core.Int(520)` gets past the pack's own layout and aborts at its argument tuple's check (unit D's record). The 2026.10.12 nightly prints 5 for c06 because it is a release build in which `BuildType`'s `CARBON_DCHECK` is compiled out, so its output is not evidence that the lowered layout is correct; `BuildPackedStructType`'s checks are `CARBON_CHECK`s that release builds keep, and the nightly aborts on the `(Core.Int(24), i32)` tuple. Scalars are fine. A fix needs the tuple (packed struct) layout for an integer whose LLVM alloc size differs from its Carbon size, as W-368 did for packs: pad or represent each such element so that offsets and the total size match the Carbon object layout. Passed to this item by unit D's record, outside its break condition: `var a: array(Core.Int(520), 3)` aborts at "Field at non-byte offset" (type.cpp:763 on trunk) on every toolchain measured. Break condition (closing): probe c06, the `(Core.Int(520),)` and `(Core.Int(24), i32)` tuples and c01 compile and run with the expected output (5, 5, 12 and 100006) on a container-built toolchain.
